memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really I who am speaking to you. Tell my father about all the honour accorded me in Egypt and about everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.'" — Gen 45:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"You can see for yourselves." Joseph wants them to be sure. Their own eyes, their own ears, his own familiar voice speaking their own language. This is not a rumour they will have to take on trust — they are eyewitnesses.

And now they are sent to be witnesses to someone else: tell my father everything you have seen. That is their commission. Not to explain it or defend it, just to report what they have seen with their own eyes.

Jacob will find it almost impossible to believe. But the brothers will not be arguing him into faith; they will simply be telling him what they witnessed, and bringing along the evidence Joseph sends with them.

That is exactly how the gospel first went out. The apostles were not clever debaters constructing a theory. They said, "We cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard" (Acts 4:20). John wrote of what he had heard, seen with his eyes and touched with his hands (1 Jn 1:1-3).

You may feel unqualified to speak about Christ. But you are not asked to be an expert. You are asked to tell people what you have seen Him do in your own life. That is a witness, and it is enough.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you personally seen God do that you could tell someone about?
2. Does the pressure to have all the answers keep you from speaking about Christ?
3. Who is waiting to hear your report?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I may not have all the answers, but I know what You have done in my life. Give me courage to simply tell what I have seen. Amen.
